hook: SCP-3300 starts as a calm report about a Montana town and a yearly stretch of bad weather, then hands the floor to a teenager's journal. Give the journal time: it opens as ordinary diary chatter about friends, a tabletop game and an overbearing mom, and the mood turns gradually. Be aware that it goes on to describe a parent beaten to death, several deaths among the friends and a suicide by shotgun, all in the first person.
whyItMatters: This is a strong example of the report-plus-found-document structure, where the official text sets the rules and the recovered text shows what living inside them feels like. The description is rich on its own: a whole population swapped out each year, a cognitohazard that dulls outsiders' attention rather than their memory, and records reaching back to the Foundation's beginnings. The journal answers almost none of the official questions, yet makes every one of them personal.
thingsToNotice:
The recurring dream is the key. It belongs to a woman in a village dying of a plague, where a boy announces that water is their salvation and the few survivors carry hundreds of their dead into a river until only they are left. In the last dream she is the storm itself, torn apart with the screaming spirits of her village and flung down to earth for a moment before being dragged back, which reads as the origin the report admits it does not know.

The waking story makes that literal. A stranger who calls her house his own beats her mother to death with a golf club pulled out of his rippling, water-filled chest; Jared boils away into steam; Mike's skull turns out to hold water instead of a brain, and when Sam cuts her own arm, water pours out of it too. Every road leads back to the town sign, silent crowds wait outside in the rain, Sam walks into them, and Isabel is reduced to a puddle. Margaret ends by hearing the rain call her its child, and her closing line repeats what Sam said on the way out, so the journal stops on her choosing to go into the water.
